stem.text: Which row correctly describes the primary structure, secondary structure, tertiary structure and quaternary structure of some proteins?

A.text: determines the folding of the polypeptide; depends on hydrogen bonding between the side-chains of amino acids; defines the overall shape and folding of the protein; formed when two or more identical polypeptides join together

B.text: defines the order of amino acids in the polypeptide; usually forms immediately after polypeptide synthesis; is held together by all the types of bonding that occur in proteins; found in globular proteins such as haemoglobin but never in fibrous proteins

C.text: involves covalent bonds only; involves interactions between –H and =O; essential for the function of enzymes and receptors; formed when two or more polypeptides join together

D.text: involves peptide bonds between the side-chains of amino acids; involves folding between local regions within a polypeptide molecule; changes reversibly when bound to non-competitive inhibitors; can involve hydrogen bonds, covalent bonds and hydrophobic interactions
